place: Any cave below the surface (rule, not a place)
notes: Rule: away from the entrances, cave air sits at about the mean annual surface temperature of the ground above at that elevation (NPS Carlsbad Caverns: caves 'tend to reflect the average annual temperature for the area at that given elevation'; NPS Great Basin: bedrock is 'often just about the average year round surface temperature'; Badino 2004, Int. J. Speleology 33: cave temperature is closely tied to the external climate, short swings filtered out by the rock). Exceptions: cold-air traps that take in winter air run colder (Carlsbad's Big Room 13 C under a 17 C surface), and depth adds geothermal warmth (Carlsbad's deepest point 20 C). Humidity: 90-100% (Lehman Caves 90-100%; Carlsbad near 100% deep inside, down to 87.5% in the Big Room in winter). Near entrances both follow the outside more. No months: no day, no season, no rain.

rule.t_mean: year mean of the surface biome above (at that elevation)

place: Djadokhta Formation, Bayan Zag (Flaming Cliffs) and Ukhaa Tolgod, southern Gobi, Mongolia
notes: Campanian, about 80-72 Ma (eolian deposition from about 80 Ma: Hasegawa et al. 2008). LITERATURE: an arid sand-dune desert of at least 160,000 km2 with large cross-bedded dunes and mature calcretes (Hasegawa et al. 2008, 2009); paleosols at Bayan Zag read as semi-arid with seasonal rain, hot dry summers and short, probably humid winters (Naugolnykh 2016); short-lived ponds and streams between dunes, and dune collapses after heavy rain (Dingus et al. 2008; Loope et al. 1999); the Okavango-Kalahari is the modern analogue (Jerzykiewicz 1998). NO published MAT or MAP for the Djadokhta was found. The nearest number is the younger, wetter Nemegt Formation (Maastrichtian, Owocki et al. 2020, from Tarbosaurus tooth enamel): a monsoonal climate with summer rain, MAP 775-835 mm, and an MAT reported as about 7.6 C on Wikipedia's summary but 'ten degrees above today's Mongolia' in the paper's abstract, so treat that MAT as unsettled. ESTIMATES (ours): MAT about 17 C (12-22), warmest month about 30 C, coldest about 5 C (half range about 12 C: a continental interior at about 40-45 N), MAP about 100-250 mm in a short summer wet season (2-3 months), and wet/dry months are a guess following the Nemegt's summer monsoon (Naugolnykh's 'humid winters' would put the rain in winter instead).
palaeolatitude: about 40-45 N (reconstructions vary; Wikipedia infoboxes give 30.7 N for the Djadokhta and 40.5 N for the Barun Goyot, both unsourced)

place: Barun Goyot (Baruungoyot) Formation, Nemegt Basin (Khulsan, Hermiin Tsav), southern Gobi, Mongolia
notes: Late Campanian to early Maastrichtian, partly coeval with the Djadokhta. LITERATURE: red eolian and interdune sandstones, transitional between the Djadokhta's dunes and the Nemegt's river plains; in the 'lithobiotope' model the Djadokhta is the arid dune habitat, the Barun Goyot the semi-arid transition and the Nemegt the wetter plains (Jerzykiewicz et al. 2021); wetness increases up through the Baruungoyot into the Nemegt (Eberth 2018). No MAT or MAP for the Barun Goyot itself was found; the Nemegt above it had summer monsoon rain and MAP 775-835 mm (Owocki et al. 2020). ESTIMATES (ours): MAT about 17 C (12-22), half range about 11 C, MAP about 250-450 mm, a summer wet season of about 3 months and a dry winter-spring.

place: Cedar Mountain Formation, Ruby Ranch Member type area and 'Lake Carpenter' near Arches, east-central Utah, USA
notes: Ruby Ranch Member, late Aptian-early Albian (about 116-110 Ma; 'Lake Carpenter' ash 115.65 Ma). LITERATURE: a semi-arid to seasonal floodplain with calcrete and vertic paleosols, carbonate concentrated by dry-season evaporation, and dolomite showing strong evaporation; aridity from the rain shadow of the Sevier highlands ('Nevadaplano') to the west (Suarez et al. 2014, J. Sed. Res. 84: 975). MAP from paleosol chemistry (Suarez et al. 2020/2021, Geol. Soc. London Spec. Publ. 498): CALMAG 736-1,042 mm, CIA-K 795-1,275 mm, a little lower during the C10 carbon-isotope event; a thesis using carbon-isotope methods got much lower values (274 and 599 mm for the member: Univ. of Arkansas). Temperatures: clumped isotopes of lake carbonate 15-31 C (calcite 27-41 C, dolomite 19-21 C), palustrine 19.8-44.5 C; these are spring-summer water temperatures, not the year mean, and values above 50 C are diagenesis (Suarez et al. 2023, 2025). Palaeolatitude about 34 N (Suarez et al. 2014). No published MAT. ESTIMATES (ours): MAT about 21 C (17-25), half range about 8 C, MAP about 800 mm (the proxies' overlap, likely high), a summer wet season of about 4 months and a winter-spring dry season of about 6 (monsoon-like, as the paleosols suggest; the exact months are a guess). Note: Utahraptor comes from the older Yellow Cat Member, now dated Berriasian-Valanginian (about 139-134 Ma, Joeckel et al. 2023), also seasonally dry with vertic paleosols, outside the 75-125 Ma window.
palaeolatitude: about 34 N (Suarez et al. 2014); Wikipedia's infobox gives 40.2 N

place: Kaiparowits Formation, Grand Staircase-Escalante, southern Utah, USA (wet coastal-plain forest of southern Laramidia)
koppen: Cwa/Aw-like humid subtropical with a dry season (estimate)
notes: Late Campanian, about 76.6-74.5 Ma. LITERATURE: alluvial to coastal plain beside the Western Interior Seaway, 'extensively ponded and annually flooded', humid and subtropical 'similar to the present-day Gulf Coast or certain areas of Southeast Asia' (Maccracken et al. 2022, PLOS ONE); 'overall wet (humid), tropical to subtropical wet-dry setting, with episodic longer dry spells' (Titus et al. 2021, PeerJ). MAT 20 +/- 1 C from leaf-margin analysis (Miller et al. 2013); paleosol carbonate clumped isotopes give warm-season soil temperatures of about 35 +/- 4 C (Burgener et al. 2019). Tyrannosaur tooth isotopes point to a monsoonal setting, compared with Hanoi and Cuiaba, with cold-season highland runoff (Yamamura et al. 2021). Roberts (2007) is quoted as 'humid, subtropical (150 cm annual precipitation)', seen only in a search snippet: UNCONFIRMED. Flora: 80+ plant morphotypes, mostly angiosperms, with ferns, a lycopod and a horsetail in the understory, and cupressaceous, podocarp and pine conifers (charcoal). A purer fern-and-conifer forest would be Early Cretaceous, but no such formation with comparable climate numbers was found. ESTIMATES (ours): half range about 8 C (coldest month about 12 C, warmest about 28 C), MAP about 1,200-1,600 mm, a wet season of about 6 summer months and a dry season of about 4 winter months (monsoonal analogues); the months themselves are a guess.
palaeolatitude: mid-latitude southern Laramidia (value not looked up)

place: High rock in the Cretaceous world: the Sevier fold-thrust highlands west of the Utah basins (ESTIMATE)
notes: ALL ESTIMATE. No palaeoclimate data for the highlands themselves. Suarez et al. (2014) tie the floodplain's dryness to the rain shadow of the Sevier highlands ('Nevadaplano'), and Yamamura et al. (2021) find cold-season highland runoff reaching the Kaiparowits rivers, so the uplands were real, wetter on their windward side and cooler. Rule used: the standard lapse rate, 6.5 C per km (the game's own temperature::air already applies 0.0065 C per block of altitude). Crags about 1-1.5 km above lowlands at 20-21 C give MAT about 12-14 C; we suggest 13 C at the crags' base, half range about 8 C, MAP about 700-1,000 mm with a summer wet season, frost and some snow on the tops in winter. If the game also lowers the air with the block's altitude, set this at the biome's base height so it is not counted twice.
